title: Several parallel readers of a sliding window with a distance penalty in the exponent
summary: The last W symbols each keep an address and a content per reader. R readers, each with its own projections of width d/R, weight the windowed contents by the exponential of a scaled probe-address match minus a reader-specific penalty proportional to the distance back. The readers' normalized outputs are concatenated and projected.
core_idea: Let R parallel readers each take an exponentially weighted, normalized mean over the last W contents, with scores equal to a scaled match minus a linear distance penalty.

state.name: Q
state.meaning: The addresses and contents of the last W symbols for all R readers; the oldest entry is dropped when a new one arrives.

update.name: append
update.latex: a^{r}_t = W^{r}_a e_t,\; c^{r}_t = W^{r}_c e_t
update.plain: for reader r = 1..R: a^r_t = W^r_a e_t and c^r_t = W^r_c e_t, each of width d/R; push them into the window and drop the entry from position t - W

readout.name: scores
readout.latex: \omega^{r}_{t,i} = \exp\left(\frac{b^{r}_t \cdot a^{r}_i}{\sqrt{d/R}} - m_r (t - i)\right),\; t - W < i \le t
readout.plain: omega^r_(t,i) = exp(b^r_t . a^r_i / sqrt(d/R) - m_r (t - i)) for the W positions in the window, probe b^r_t = W^r_b e_t, fixed slope m_r = 2^(-r)

readout.name: readers
readout.plain: y^r_t = sum_i omega^r_(t,i) c^r_i / sum_j omega^r_(t,j); y_t = W_o concatenation of the R readers

readout.name: symbol
readout.plain: next symbol scores O y_t over the V symbols

learning.description: Every matrix and offset is learned by gradient descent on the cross-entropy of the next symbol over a training corpus, with backpropagation through the whole sequence.
learning.few_shot_argument: No structure for few examples; about 1500 training sequences are needed for recall of 4 pairs within the window.

complexity.total_sequence: Theta(n W d + n d^2 + n d V)
complexity.constants_notes: Each reader matches W addresses of width d/R, so the window read costs W d per symbol over all readers; the buffer holds 2 W d numbers.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Gradient descent with no structure for few examples.

prediction.statement: From random weights, 1500 training sequences of 4 pairs over 16 symbols, all inside the window, give recall accuracy 0.99.

capabilities.prediction: Exact with hand-set weights when all K pairs lie inside the last W symbols; pairs older than W are lost.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: Exact for 2L + 1 <= W with hand-set position matching; impossible when the string has left the window.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: A pair written more than W symbols before its probe is recalled above chance.
The counted operations grow faster than linearly in n at fixed W.

toy_example.description: One reader with W = 3 and slope 0.5 over a window of three entries.
toy_example.python:
import json, math
A = [[1.0, 0.0], [1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]]
Cv = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
b = [1.0, 0.0]
t = 3
m = 0.5
w = [math.exp((b[0] * A[i][0] + b[1] * A[i][1]) / math.sqrt(2.0) - m * (t - (i + 1))) for i in range(3)]
y = sum(w[i] * Cv[i] for i in range(3)) / sum(w)
print(json.dumps({"read": round(y, 6), "weights": [round(v / sum(w), 6) for v in w]}))
